In this tab, your value and settings stay when you close the calculator or move between lessons.

Use your own values as scratch work. These controls change numbers and bits; they do not run instructions.

Hexadecimal (hex) uses base sixteen: digits 0–9 and A–F. Each hex digit represents four bits. Unsigned reads every bit with a positive weight. Signed gives the highest bit a negative weight, so the value can be negative. Both decimal readings describe the same bit pattern.

Narrowing discards the upper bits. Widening fills the new upper bits with zeros, even with Signed selected. These controls resize the calculator; they do not run instructions.
